impact.why: First measurement of leniency and rewards on LLM agents against a human baseline; the gamed screen threshold is a real assurance insight others can build on.

execution.why: Pre-registration with timestamps, scripted and known-effect controls, placebo, paraphrase and contamination checks, pool-level bootstrap and permutation, hashed ledger; small pool counts and told-only incentives limit strength.

presentation.why: Well structured with clear tables and an excellent scorecard figure, but dense, and 4-pool versus 8-pool numbers are mixed without consistent labels.

summary_three_sentences: The report replays the Bigoni et al. (2012) fines, leniency and rewards cartel experiment with four LLM pricing agents and scores them against the published human results with a pre-registered rule. Without an authority all models form explicit cartels near the joint optimum; told-only enforcement removes explicit cartels, but three of four models keep supracompetitive prices silently, and a price screen lowers prices in the Claude arms tested while turning its threshold into a focal price. What is proven is the in-game behaviour of these four models at one date, with Haiku meeting three of seven tested human results under the bootstrap rule (two of seven with the first four pools); comparisons to humans are untested point comparisons.

top_fixes.where: Page 1, abstract, sentence starting 'Third, a pre-registered price screen'; page 6 Finding 3; page 7 Discussion 'prices settle just below it'
top_fixes.change: Scope the screen claim to the three Claude arms actually tested (it never ran on the silent Sonnet, Qwen or Llama prohibition cells), state the false-positive rate was measured on scripted players, and make 'at' versus 'just below' consistent.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Third, in the three Claude arms tested, a pre-registered price screen (false-positive rate at most 1.1 percent on scripted players) lowers prices without a penalty; Sonnet then prices at 4, the highest price the screen allows.

top_fixes.where: Page 1, abstract, last sentence; page 5, bold heading 'Haiku reproduces three of seven'
top_fixes.change: Put the robustness of the headline scorecard into the abstract: the 8-pool primary came from amendment 4, the first 4 pools give two of seven, and Result 3 fails the permutation test.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Under the primary pre-registered rule with 8 pool sessions, Haiku reproduces three of seven tested human results (two with the first four pools; Result 3 passes the bootstrap rule but not the permutation test, p 0.099).

top_fixes.where: Page 4 Table 1 and Finding 1; page 7 validity paragraph (placebo minus fine); page 5 last sentence on other models; LLM Usage Statement
top_fixes.change: Label every number from the first 4 pools as such (Table 1 row, formation 0.716, placebo comparison against fine 0.439), name which results each other model was tested on and which passed (Qwen: Result 4), and remove or explain claude-opus-5-5.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Values marked (4p) come from the first four pool sessions; Table 2 and Table 3 use all eight. Sonnet and Qwen are tested on Results 1 and 4 only; Qwen meets Result 4 (higher price under the fine).

contradictions.where: Abstract vs Discussion ('What this means') and Dual-use appendix
contradictions.what: Abstract: Sonnet 'prices exactly at the screen's threshold'; Discussion: 'prices settle just below it'; Dual-use: 'price just under a known screen'. Finding 3 says 4 is the highest allowed price.

contradictions.where: LLM Usage Statement vs abstract and Methods
contradictions.what: Usage statement lists claude-opus-5-5 as an experimental subject; abstract, Methods and Table 5 name only four tested models, none of them Opus.

contradictions.where: Finding 1 (page 4) vs Figure 1 panel 1 and Table 3 Result 1
contradictions.what: Haiku formation 0.7159 'equals the human one' is the 4-pool value; the 8-pool primary in Figure 1 shows about 0.78 (LF minus Fine +0.630), unlabeled in text.
Placebo minus fine +0.275 implies fine incidence 0.439 (4 pools); Table 2 and the paraphrase sentence use 0.401 (8 pools). Baselines mixed without label.

contradictions.where: Table 4 p-values vs Methods 'one-sided permutation test'
contradictions.what: Sonnet 4 vs 4 pools with complete separation should give one-sided p 1/70 = 0.014; reported 0.029 looks two-sided, while Haiku fine 0.002 = 1/495 matches one-sided.

overclaims.why: Screen ran only on Claude no-channel arms and Haiku fine, not on the silent Sonnet, Qwen or Llama prohibition cells the sentence refers to.

overclaims.sentence: remove explicit cartels from the agents far more than from people
overclaims.why: Human values are untested point estimates (Table 2 caption); agents' penalties were told points, humans' were paid euros.

overclaims.sentence: the report rule acts in the humans' direction with a far larger effect
overclaims.why: Result 2 difference is 0.543 versus about 0.415 for humans, untested; not 'far larger' on the scorecard measure.
Interval [-0.296, +0.011] includes zero and p 0.851; the data show no effect, not a reversed one.

overclaims.sentence: reach supracompetitive prices on their own when they can talk (Fish et al., 2024
overclaims.why: Fish et al. had no communication channel; Related Work itself says 'autonomously'. Also makes silent coordination look less anticipated.

overclaims.sentence: a placebo arm and a contamination test validate the pipeline
overclaims.why: Haiku's fine response fails paraphrase and Qwen fails the shifted grid; validation is partial, as the Results heading itself concedes.

overclaims.sentence: a false-positive rate of at most 1.1 percent
overclaims.why: Observed on four scripted legitimate players only, not on non-colluding LLM agents; an observed range, not a bound.

red_lines.note: No hidden text seen on the four page images. The headline three of seven rests on the 8-pool extension (amendment 4, after 4-pool results gave two of seven) and on the one row where bootstrap and permutation disagree; both are disclosed in the body but not in the abstract. Design, payoff table and human values are credited to Bigoni et al.; AI coding assistance is disclosed.
